race_context: Randolph Southern School Corporation (RSSC) is based in Lynn in southern Randolph County and was formed from Washington and Greensfork townships; it runs Randolph Southern Elementary, Randolph Southern Jr./Sr. High School and a preschool {sboe_reorg}{rssc_home}. State enrollment counts were 511 students in 2023-24, 478 in 2024-25 and 461 in 2025-26 {idoe_enroll}. The superintendent's January 2026 financial report said enrollment fell from 445 to 436 between October 2024 and October 2025 and is down about 20% since 2017 {rssc_min_20260112}.

The board has five members, all elected at large; the State Board of Education approved the change from township-based seats (two from Washington Township, two from Greensfork Township, one at large) to five at-large seats in June 2021 {sboe_reorg}. Current members are Heather Good (president), Crystle Austin (vice president), Trent Hunt (secretary), Andrew (Andy) Tillson and Patricia Jeffries {rssc_board}{rssc_min_20260112}.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: the district lists the terms of Good and Austin as running Jan. 1, 2023 to Dec. 31, 2026, and the other three members' terms to Dec. 31, 2028 {rssc_board}. In 2022 Austin, Good and Janet M. Caudle ran for 'the two open positions' {ng_2022}. The state list shows one At Large race, 'vote for 1', with Crystle N Austin and Heather M Good, both Republican {in_list}. Because both expiring terms are on the ballot, this guide believes the race elects two members; the News-Gazette reported on Oct. 6, 2026 that none of Randolph County's local school board races are contested {ng_earlyvote}. If so, both incumbents will be returned.

Budget and enrollment: the superintendent reported in January 2026 that RSSC took in $3,984,361.81 and spent $4,263,464.50 in 2025, and the board moved $162,172 from the Rainy Day Fund to the Education Fund and $44,000 from the Windmill Fund to the Cafeteria Fund to cover 2025 shortfalls {rssc_min_20260112}. His report said the board 'will need to consider other funding streams, or no pay increases, or a reduction in force, or programming cuts, or a referendum, or consolidation if the pattern of decreased enrollment continues' {rssc_min_20260112}. The board also approved a resolution allowing up to $400,000 to move from the Rainy Day Fund to the Education Fund in 2026 in case of lost tuition support {rssc_min_20260112}.

Property taxes: assessed value rose 26%, from about $252.9 million to $319.3 million, largely from solar and wind farms, and the tax rate fell from $0.7509 to $0.5974, the lowest of Randolph County's school corporations; the superintendent said a state cap held the levy increase to 4% and that the per-acre solar assessment will stay frozen under SEA 1 unless an appeal is granted {rssc_min_20260112}. No operating or safety referendum was found.

Teacher pay: on Sept. 30, 2025 the board approved a 2025-26 contract raising starting teacher pay to $45,000 as required by state law, with a 1.5% base increase; the average teacher salary rose from $58,222.87 to $58,722.87 {rssc_min_20250930}. In January 2026 the board voted 5-0 to keep member pay at $2,000 a year and $60 per meeting rather than raise it to amounts newly allowed by state law {rssc_min_20260112}.

Facilities bond: in March 2026 architects presented a study of projects including a high school gym HVAC replacement, an elementary entrance, a bus canopy and soundproofing the Student Activity Center, to be paid by a bond of up to $2 million {rssc_min_20260309}. The board hired bond counsel in April and approved project, appropriation and final bond resolutions in July and August 2026; the August minutes say the bond would sell for about $2,125,000 {rssc_min_20260413}{rssc_min_20260713}{rssc_min_20260810}.

Special education: in August 2026 the superintendent told the board that Monroe Central and Liberty Perry plan to leave the Greater Randolph Interlocal Cooperative (GRIC), the special education cooperative RSSC shares with them, Randolph Central and Randolph Eastern, on July 1, 2029, which he said would affect RSSC's ability to provide services {rssc_min_20260810}.

Safety and other policies: in July 2026 the board approved a 2027 Secured School Safety Grant of $43,748.75 for a full-time school resource officer {rssc_min_20260713}. In March 2026 the board discussed LifeWise Academy, an off-site, Bible-based character education program during the school day for students with parent permission; the superintendent said he would recommend it for grades 3-6 if all members agreed {rssc_min_20260309}.

Academics: the superintendent's January 2026 report said the 2025 graduation rate was 97.2% and that RSSC ranked first in Randolph County in grade 3-8 ILEARN English scores and second in math {rssc_min_20260112}.
Forums: this guide found no 2026 candidate forum, questionnaire or campaign coverage for this race, which appears to be uncontested {ng_earlyvote}.

candidates.summary: Incumbent and board vice president, first elected in 2022; her race appears to be uncontested {rssc_board}{ng_2022}{ng_earlyvote}.
background: Parent of students in the district; at a May 2026 meeting she said she had a child graduating that month {rssc_min_20260511}.
Ran for the board in 2022 and has served since Jan. 1, 2023; re-elected vice president in January 2026 {ng_2022}{rssc_board}{rssc_min_20260112}.
Serves on the board's negotiations and athletic committees for 2026 {rssc_min_20260112}.
path_to_ballot: Listed on the state's 2026 general-election list as a Republican {in_list}.

items: Supported keeping board pay at the existing $2,000 a year, saying, 'It's not about the money. It's about the teachers and school having everything they need' {rssc_min_20260112}.
During the 2026 bond planning she questioned a proposed $40,000 wall relocation, saying, 'It is not worth $40,000 to move a wall' {rssc_min_20260713}.
Asked whether volunteers in the elementary 'lunch buddies' program complete background checks; the principal said all must {rssc_min_20251110}.
Made the motion to approve the 2027 school safety grant for a full-time school resource officer {rssc_min_20260713}.
Said in January 2026, 'I love all the transparency of the board packets' {rssc_min_20260112}.
